INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  Library Board
  MINUTES – September 22, 2021

The Inglewood Library Board met on September 22, 2021 via Zoom. The meeting was called to order at 4:31 p.m.
by Board Member Julie Minton.

Roll Call

Present:
  Julie Minton – District 1 Board Member, Vice Chairman
  Pat Douglas – District 2 Board Member
  Ernesto Castillo – District 3 Board Member
  Jacqueline Cochran – District 4 Board Member

Absent Board Members:
  Patt Sanders – At Large Board Member, Chairman

Staff:
  Kerri Arroyo – Library Manager
  Irina Martirosian – Staff Assistant

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Board Member Minton made a motion for the approval of the minutes for August 25, 2021
  Board Member Douglas seconded the motion. Minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Library Board Members Minton, Douglas and Castillo
  Nays: None

Library Report

  Library Manager, Kerri Arroyo updated the board members on the Library's programming,
  accomplishments, professional development and improvements.

  From 100% virtual summer reading program we had 193 participants, 355 completed activities, 235 hours
  of reading. We gave away 5 bikes for grand prizes, weekly prizes and grab-n-go kits. From 100% virtual
  programming we are slowly transitioning to on site programming. There will always be a virtual component
  to our programming. Once a month we are having English and bilingual story times on the lawn (civic
  center), along with giveaways and refreshments. We have fun things planned for November and
  1
   December, and have quality adult, teen and children grab-n-go kits available for holidays and provide
  activity bags for all programs. We are partnering with Downtown Los Angeles Music Center, and will
  feature mariachi dance at the Crenshaw-Imperial Branch, and a jazz concert outside of the Main library. We
  are also partnering with West LA College, where our associate librarian is a teacher’s assistant with
  noncredit classes for adults and special needs patrons. Our librarians are currently teaching basic
  computer classes at the Senior Center Mondays and Wednesdays from 10 a.m. to 12 p.m., 12 p.m. to 2
  p.m. one on one assistance.

  Library Manager, Kerri Arroyo also informed board members about partnering with Crystal Stars, Inc. Head
  Start which provides free childcare. Their newsletter has 30,000 recipients. We have 5000 plus and
  are trying to get to 6000, and with their help we will increase our patronage, readership and marketing of
  our programs and offerings. Library has purchased 8000 printed books and over $30,000 worth of audio
  books and e-books; also, added several new databases like NoveList Plus, Digitalia.

  We are working on professional development. Our staff will have access to unlimited online classes and
  workshops to increase their skills, and get certified which will allow them to do their job more efficiently.

  We are trying to rebuild our relationship with the IUSD, private and charter schools, and teachers. Our
  librarians are having class visits not only virtually, but also on-site.

  We did a survey and from a total of 114 surveys, 83% were satisfied with our services; computers, printing
  services, borrowing materials and passport services. 35 % of patrons want the library to be open on
  Sundays.

  Board member Minton asked how long the survey was conducted and if we are having problems with
  people wearing masks.

  Library Manager, Kerri Arroyo answered that the survey was conducted for 4 weeks and the goal was to
  get 40 to 80 responses, but ended up having 114. The mask requirement is a very high priority and with
  the help of security, our staff ensures that the mask mandate is enforced.

  We received 2 new large media/book drops with our library logo on it, one for the Main Library and one for
  the Crenshaw-Imperial Branch, both were installed this month.

  We are approved for the Morningside Park Branch renovation, it will begin in December. Crenshaw-
  Imperial Branch just had all new carpeting, new signage, and working on giving a new vibrant look to
  the patio, because it’s used for the lunch program and for outdoor programming.

  Kerri Arroyo also gave a shout out to our librarians, support staff, clerks, supervisors who are the front line
  of all interaction and received five stars from patrons who are coming on site and on google.

Public Comments

  None

  2
 Friends Report

  Susan Carleo, President of the Friends of Inglewood Public Library (FOIPL) informed the library board
about getting donations and preparing for a big December book sale. They have an ongoing process of cleaning,
categorizing, choosing books on a weekly basis. FOIPL received $16 dollars from Amazon Smile last month. They
are still working on their website and hopefully will be ready soon. FOIPL is delighted to see all the changes that are
happening in the library and having Kerri as a Library Manager. Sue Carleo thanked Kerri Arroyo for all the support
that they are getting from her and the library staff. Also, Sue Carleo mentioned that due to a conflict in their
schedule they might not be able to attend the October board meeting.

Public Comments

  None

Commissioner Comments

  Board member Douglas was very pleased with the progress.
  Board member Castillo thanked Kerri Arroyo for the power point presentation and mention that graphics are
  amazing on our newsletter. He’s very happy to hear that the library is working with schools, providing all the
  recourses, partnerships, as Inglewood is moving forward.
  Board member Cochran asked Kerri to email the power point presentation, love the grab and goes, was
  excited about the Morningside Library renovation and will go to Crenshaw Library to see the new carpeting.
  Board member Minton was floored about the Morningside library and liked everything about library report.
  All Board members thanked Kerri Arroyo and were very happy with the library report.

  With no further comments the meeting was adjourned at 5:17 p.m.
